key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning outperformed the multitask neural network on all three welding targets, with the largest accuracy gain in ultimate tensile strength (UTS).
engineering_relevance: Predicting UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected zone (HAZ) hardness can support welding process assessment and welded-component quality control.
method: Train a multitask neural network with shared representations and task-specific outputs.
Compare against stacking ensemble learning using the same dataset.
Evaluate each target using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved R² values of 0.9863, 0.9782, and 0.8453 for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, respectively, versus 0.6724, 0.9215, and 0.8407 for the multitask network.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE scaling, limiting assessment of deployment readiness and physical error magnitudes.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
